summary: Saturn in Aries is debilitated (deepest at 20 degrees) in the sign of an enemy, Mars. Patience and structure meet impulse and haste, so the classical picture is friction, restlessness and strained relationships, which later authors say can be transformed when the debilitation is cancelled.
common_outcomes: Hardship through hard labour and one's own habits; ill temper; friction with relatives and one's own people (Saravali 29.1-2; Raman HPA ch.22)
Restless, wandering and friendless tendencies (Brihat Jataka 18.17; Raman HPA ch.22)
Limited means and loss of position or dependence during the planet's dasa (Saravali 29.1-2; Phaladeepika 9.18 on debilitated planets)
Raman describes Saturn's dasa from Aries as a period of losses, disappointments and strained relations (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.17 lists foolishness, wandering and deceit as Aries-specific traits
Saravali 29.29: a Jupiter aspect on Saturn in a Mars sign gives happiness, wealth and a minister's or chief's position; 29.25: a Sun aspect gives farming and livestock wealth
Frawley: Saturn in Aries with its debility cancelled can give strong leadership and strength of will

by_area.personality: Classical and modern sign lists describe temper, impatience and resentment (Saravali 29.1-2; Raman HPA ch.22); with cancelled debility, strength of will (Frawley p.126).
by_area.career: Hard labour and work under others (Saravali 29.1-2); Braha describes Saturn in Aries in the 10th house as an uphill professional struggle.
by_area.finance: Limited means in classical texts (Saravali 29.1-2); a Jupiter aspect reverses this (Saravali 29.29).
by_area.relationships: Friction with one's own people and relatives (Saravali 29.1-2; Raman HPA ch.24).
by_area.family: Saravali 29.1-2 says inimical to relatives; Raman's dasa note adds misunderstandings with relatives and friends (HPA ch.24).

strengtheners: Cancelled debility (neecha bhanga): Saturn in an angle from the lagna or Moon, Mars (lord of Aries) exalted or strong, or a planet exalted in Saturn's own signs (e.g. Mars in Capricorn); Frawley says at least two such factors are needed (Astrology of the Seers pp.126-127)
Jupiter aspecting Saturn in a Mars sign (Saravali 29.29)
Sun aspect gives agricultural and livestock wealth (Saravali 29.25)
Retrograde Saturn: Phaladeepika 9.20 says a retrograde planet gives results like exaltation; Frawley counts retrogression only a minor cancelling factor
weakeners_or_cancellations: Moon, Mars, Mercury or Venus aspect on Saturn in a Mars sign is described negatively (Saravali 29.26-28, 29.30)
Combustion weakens a planet in its dasa (Phaladeepika 9.19)
If Mars is exalted in Capricorn while Saturn is debilitated in Aries, each rules the other's sign and their effects tend to neutralise, the stronger one prevailing (Frawley p.127)
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there; Raman (HPA ch.17) lists Saturn as ill-disposed for Aries, Leo and Pisces lagnas. Braha describes Saturn in Aries rising as a hard start in life and in the 10th house as professional struggle; these lagna-specific readings still depend on cancellation factors.

source_views.view: Saturn in Aries: miserable through vices and hard labour, deceitful, hates relatives, garrulous, poor, ill-tempered, inimical to his own people, does base acts.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.17 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Saturn in Aries: foolish, restless, deceitful, friendless.
Saturn's exaltation is Libra; the seventh sign (Aries) is its debilitation, at the same degree (20).

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara ch.15 v.7 'Planetary rulerships' (English compilation by Ramapriya, archive.org)
source_views.view: For Saturn, Aries is inimical and the place of debilitation.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.18, 9.20 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: A debilitated planet brings loss of position, debts and dependence in its dasa; a retrograde planet acts as if exalted.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.22 'Planets in Different Rasis', Saturn (pp.132-134)
source_views.view: Saturn in Aries: insincere, peevish, resentful, quarrelsome, gloomy, wandering, misunderstood.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.24, Saturn's dasa by sign (pp.158-159)
source_views.view: Saturn's dasa with Saturn in Aries: unexpected losses, disappointments in undertakings, misunderstandings with relatives and friends, more enemies.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers pp.125-127 'Exaltation and Debility' (archive.org)
source_views.view: Neecha bhanga factors: angle from lagna or Moon, exalted or strong dispositor, a planet exalted in a sign the debilitated planet rules, retrogression (minor); two needed. Saturn in Aries cancelled gives leadership and will.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer, chapter on Saturn and Saturn-in-houses dignity notes (archive.org scan)
source_views.view: Saturn works worst in Aries, its fall; in the 1st or 10th house in Aries it describes a hard start and professional struggle.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Saturn (commentary on Saturn's 108 names, archive.org)
source_views.view: Commentary on name 73: Saturn is debilitated in Bharani (Aries), and when Saturn is weak, keeping order in life is harder.

disagreements: Classical texts (Saravali, Brihat Jataka) and Raman's sign list are uniformly harsh. Frawley and the neecha bhanga rules allow a cancelled debility to give leadership and will; Phaladeepika 9.20 treats a retrograde planet as exalted, while Frawley counts retrogression only a minor factor. Authors differ on how many cancelling factors are needed.
phrasing_guidance: Present as a placement where patience is learned through friction, not as a curse. Always check for cancellation before describing it as weak. Avoid words like 'foolish' or 'deceitful' for the person; say 'may be tested around impatience or trust'. No health or longevity predictions.

summary: Saturn in Taurus sits in the sign of its friend Venus. Classical texts describe a serving or dependent position, modest means and attraction to pleasure, while Raman's modern list adds success, cleverness and self-restraint, and his dasa note speaks of good income.
common_outcomes: Service or dependent work and many assignments (Saravali 29.3-4)
Strong attraction to partners and pleasure (Saravali 29.3-4; Brihat Jataka 18.18)
Raman lists success, power, cleverness, persuasiveness, love of solitude and self-restraint (HPA ch.22)
Raman's dasa note: gains from land and agriculture and good income (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.18 mentions limited power and several marriages

Saravali 29.32: Moon aspect brings wealth through women and honour from ministers; 29.35: Jupiter aspect makes one liked, charitable and industrious; 29.36: Venus aspect brings gems, strength and royal favour
Saravali 29.31: Sun aspect makes one learned but losing wealth

by_area.personality: Raman: clever, persuasive, likes solitude, self-restrained but a worrier (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Service and many assignments (Saravali 29.3-4); agriculture and land gains in Saturn's dasa (Raman HPA ch.24).
by_area.finance: Saravali 29.3-4 says bereft of wealth; Raman's dasa note gives great income (HPA ch.24); benefic aspects improve wealth (Saravali 29.32, 29.36).
by_area.relationships: Classical texts flag attraction to women and several unions (Saravali 29.3-4; Brihat Jataka 18.18).

strengtheners: Venus is Saturn's friend (Braha; Bhavartha Ratnakara 15.7 lists Taurus as friendly for Saturn)
Moon, Jupiter or Venus aspecting Saturn (Saravali 29.32, 29.35, 29.36)
Phaladeepika 9.16: a planet in a friend's sign brings success through friends and support
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mercury aspect is described as weakening and base (Saravali 29.34)
Sun aspect costs wealth (Saravali 29.31)
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there. For Taurus lagna this places the yogakaraka in the lagna itself.

source_views.source: Saravali 29.3-4 (English e-text on archive.org whose chapter captions and wording match R. Santhanam's translation; translator not named in the file)
source_views.view: Saturn in Taurus: bereft of wealth, a servant, untruthful speech, bad friends, attached to women, strong sight, many assignments.

source_views.view: Saturn in Taurus or Libra aspected by the Sun: learned but loses wealth; Moon: wealth through women, honoured by ministers; Mars: skilled in war preparations, talkative, wealthy; Mercury: jocular, base; Jupiter: liked, charitable, industrious; Venus: gems, strong, dear to the king.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.18 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Saturn in Taurus: limited power, strong attraction to partners, several marriages.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara ch.15 v.7 'Planetary rulerships' (English compilation by Ramapriya, archive.org)
source_views.view: For Saturn, Taurus and Gemini are friendly signs.

source_views.source: Phaladeepika 9.16
source_views.view: A planet in a friend's sign gives success through friends, family and wealth.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.22 'Planets in Different Rasis', Saturn (pp.132-134)
source_views.view: Saturn in Taurus: deceitful, successful, powerful, unorthodox, clever, likes solitude, persuasive, self-restrained, worried.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.24, Saturn's dasa by sign (pp.158-159)
source_views.view: Saturn's dasa from Taurus: success in agriculture and with livestock, great income, access to things desired.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer, chapter on Saturn and Saturn-in-houses dignity notes (archive.org scan)
source_views.view: Saturn's friends are Mercury and Venus, who welcome it in their signs.

disagreements: Saravali calls the native poor; Raman's sign list calls him successful and powerful and his dasa note promises income. The friendly-sign rule (Phaladeepika, Bhavartha Ratnakara, Braha) supports the more favourable reading.
phrasing_guidance: Emphasise patient building of security and the need for discipline with comfort. Do not predict infidelity or multiple marriages; say relationships benefit from clear commitments.

summary: Saturn in Gemini is in the sign of its friend Mercury. Classical verses warn of debts, toil and restraint, while Raman's modern list adds an original, strategic and scientific mind, and his dasa note speaks of recognition and trade profits.
common_outcomes: Debts, confinement and toil (Saravali 29.5-6)
Wandering nature (Saravali 29.5-6; Raman HPA ch.22)
Original, subtle, strategic and logical mind with a taste for chemical and mechanical sciences (Raman HPA ch.22)
Raman's dasa note: recognition of services, trade profits and respect from rulers (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.17: in Mercury's signs, lacking modesty, comfort or wealth and uneven in writing or painting

Saravali 29.40: Mercury aspect gives wealth and skill in dance, music and arts; 29.41: Jupiter aspect makes one trusted in the king's circle; 29.38: Moon aspect gives king-like standing and honour through women
Saravali 29.5-6 also mentions devotion through hymns and prayers

by_area.personality: Raman: original, subtle, ingenious, strategic, logical, sometimes narrow-minded (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Chemical and mechanical sciences (Raman HPA ch.22); recognition and trade profits in Saturn's dasa (Raman HPA ch.24).
by_area.finance: Saravali 29.5-6 warns of debts; Raman's dasa note gives profits in trade and speculation (HPA ch.24).
by_area.spirituality: Saravali 29.5-6 mentions consecration through hymns and prayers.

strengtheners: Mercury is Saturn's friend (Braha; Bhavartha Ratnakara 15.7)
Mercury or Jupiter aspecting Saturn (Saravali 29.40-41)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars aspect: heavy loads and dullness (Saravali 29.39)
Sun aspect: virtuous and enduring but without happiness or wealth (Saravali 29.37)
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) says that for Gemini lagna Venus joined with Saturn in good signs gives an excellent career; Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there.

source_views.source: Saravali 29.5-6 (English e-text on archive.org whose chapter captions and wording match R. Santhanam's translation; translator not named in the file)
source_views.view: Saturn in Gemini: debts and imprisonment, toil, vanity, consecrates by hymns and prayers, keeps hidden, cunning, fond of wandering and sports.

source_views.view: Saturn in Gemini or Virgo aspected by the Sun: virtuous, enduring, without wealth; Moon: king-like, honour through women; Mars: carries heavy loads; Mercury: rich, skilled in dance, song and arts; Jupiter: trusted in the king's circle; Venus: teacher of yoga or saint.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.17 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: In Mercury's signs: lacks modesty, comfort, wealth and children; uneven in writing or painting.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara ch.15 v.7 'Planetary rulerships' (English compilation by Ramapriya, archive.org)
source_views.view: For Saturn, Gemini is a friendly sign.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.22 'Planets in Different Rasis', Saturn (pp.132-134)
source_views.view: Saturn in Gemini: wandering, untidy, original, subtle, ingenious, strategic, few children, taste for chemical and mechanical sciences, logical, speculative.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.24, Saturn's dasa by sign (pp.158-159)
source_views.view: Saturn's dasa from Gemini: recognition of services, humanitarian work, profits in trade and speculation, respect from rulers, reputation.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer, chapter on Saturn and Saturn-in-houses dignity notes (archive.org scan)
source_views.view: Mercury is one of Saturn's friends.

disagreements: Saravali and Brihat Jataka are negative; Raman's modern sign list and dasa note are mixed to favourable. Brihat Jataka treats Gemini and Virgo together; Saravali gives them separate verses but shared aspect verses.
phrasing_guidance: Describe as a careful, serious mind that does well with structure; mention obligations or debts only as areas to manage. Avoid predicting legal trouble.

summary: Saturn in Cancer is in the sign of the Moon, a natural enemy. Classical texts link it with poverty in youth, distance from the mother and quarrels with kin, but Saravali adds learning, soft speech and a king-like position in mid-life; Foss sees Cancer's caring nature as improving Saturn.
common_outcomes: Lack of wealth in boyhood with improvement and a king-like position in mid-life (Saravali 29.7-8)
Distance from the mother or lack of motherly care (Saravali 29.7-8; Brihat Jataka 18.18; Raman HPA ch.22)
Friction with relatives (Saravali 29.7-8; Raman HPA ch.24)
Learned and soft-spoken (Saravali 29.7-8)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.7-8 also gives a beloved wife
Saravali 29.47: Jupiter aspect gives lands, houses, friends, sons, wealth and gems; 29.45: Mars aspect gives royal wealth but a difficult circle; 29.43: Sun aspect is the hardest
Brihat Jataka 18.18 adds childlessness and poverty

by_area.personality: Soft-spoken and learned (Saravali 29.7-8); Raman lists slow, stubborn and selfish traits (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Distinguished in action and king-like in mid-life (Saravali 29.7-8).
by_area.finance: Poor in youth, improving later (Saravali 29.7-8); Jupiter aspect brings property and wealth (Saravali 29.47).
by_area.family: Distance from mother and quarrels with kin are classical themes (Saravali 29.7-8; Brihat Jataka 18.18); Raman's dasa note adds family strife (HPA ch.24).

strengtheners: Jupiter aspect (Saravali 29.47)
Mercury aspect: conquers enemies and does noble acts (Saravali 29.46)
Retrograde Saturn (Phaladeepika 9.20)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Sun aspect (Saravali 29.43) is described as the most difficult
Phaladeepika 9.17: a planet in an enemy's sign brings dependence and opposition in its dasa
Frawley: non-watery planets such as Saturn in water signs tend to negate the water element, and can be overpowered by it if weak (p.115)
lagna_or_context_notes: Foss notes that Saturn in Cancer in the 1st house (examples: Indira Gandhi, G.W. Bush) is generally improved by Cancer's sattvic, caring nature. Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there.

source_views.view: Saturn in Cancer: beloved wife, no wealth in boyhood, learned, motherless, soft-spoken, distinguished in acts, inimical to relatives, kingly in mid-life with growing pleasures; also frequent illness (a theme not to be predicted).

source_views.view: Saturn in Cancer aspected by the Sun: hardship; Moon: wealthy but trouble with siblings; Mars: royal wealth, gold and gems; Mercury: conquers enemies, noble acts; Jupiter: lands, houses, friends, sons, wealth; Venus: noble descent but little happiness.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.18 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Saturn in Cancer: poverty, separation from mother, childlessness, lack of learning.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara ch.15 v.7 'Planetary rulerships' (English compilation by Ramapriya, archive.org)
source_views.view: For Saturn, Cancer and Leo are inimical signs.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.24, Saturn's dasa by sign (pp.158-159)
source_views.view: Saturn's dasa from Cancer: family strife, more enemies, trouble from relatives, physical and mental strain.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Saturn (commentary on Saturn's 108 names, archive.org)
source_views.view: Commentary on name 19: Saturn in Cancer in the 1st is generally improved by Cancer's sattvic nature; a royal sign that cares.

source_views.source: David Frawley, The Astrology of the Seers p.115
source_views.view: Non-watery planets (Mars, Saturn, Sun, nodes) in water signs may negate the water element, or be overpowered by it if weak.

disagreements: Brihat Jataka says lacking learning; Saravali says learned and king-like in mid-life. Raman's dasa note is harsh, while Foss reads Cancer as improving Saturn. All agree on early domestic hardship and the mother theme.
phrasing_guidance: Speak of emotional responsibility and a slow-building sense of security. Never predict a parent's death or childlessness; say 'the relationship with mother or home may carry responsibility or distance'.

summary: Saturn in Leo is in the sign of its chief enemy, the Sun. Texts describe toil, servitude and strained close relationships, alongside skill and interest in writing and reading; Raman calls it a hard-working, good writer.
common_outcomes: Heavy work and toil before recognition (Saravali 29.9-10; Brihat Jataka 18.18; Raman HPA ch.22)
Interest and skill in writing and reading (Saravali 29.9-10; Raman HPA ch.22: good writer)
Strained ties with spouse, children or one's own people (Saravali 29.9-10; Brihat Jataka 18.18)
Raman's dasa note: uneasiness, distrust and disappointment (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.53: Jupiter aspect makes one chief and rich in his town or among his people, with children; 29.50: Moon aspect gives wealth, fame and royal favour; 29.54: Venus aspect gives splendour, wealth and a good end; 29.49 (Sun) and 29.51 (Mars) aspects give hardship
Brihat Jataka 18.18: coarse conduct and trouble through offspring

by_area.personality: Raman: severe, obstinate, hard-working (HPA ch.22); Saravali 29.9-10 adds ill temper and strong desires.
by_area.career: Service and heavy labour (Saravali 29.9-10); writing and reading (Saravali 29.9-10; Raman HPA ch.22).
by_area.finance: Improves with Moon, Jupiter or Venus aspect (Saravali 29.50, 29.53, 29.54).
by_area.relationships: Saravali 29.9-10 says devoid of wife or of one's own people; present only as strain to work on.
by_area.family: Few sons (Raman HPA ch.22); trouble through children (Brihat Jataka 18.18).

strengtheners: Jupiter, Moon or Venus aspect on Saturn (Saravali 29.50, 29.53, 29.54)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Sun aspect (Saravali 29.49), Mars aspect (29.51) and Mercury aspect (29.52)
Phaladeepika 9.17 on enemy-sign placement
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) lists Saturn as ill-disposed for Aries, Leo and Pisces lagnas; for Leo lagna Saturn rising here combines both. Braha says that for Taurus lagna (Saturn in the 4th, i.e. Leo) Saturn gives happiness and fixed assets, especially real estate.

source_views.view: Saturn in Leo: interested in writing and reading, skilful, disdained, devoid of wife and own men, lives by servitude, ill-tempered, carries loads, toils hard.

source_views.view: For Saturn, Leo is inimical.

source_views.view: Saturn in Leo: severe, obstinate, few sons, unfortunate, conflicting, hard worker, good writer.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.24, Saturn's dasa by sign (pp.158-159)
source_views.view: Saturn's dasa from Leo: uneasiness, distrust, disappointments, unrest, money troubles if afflicted.

source_views.source: James Braha, Ancient Hindu Astrology for the Modern Western Astrologer, chapter on Saturn and Saturn-in-houses dignity notes (archive.org scan)
source_views.view: For Taurus and Libra ascendants Saturn in the 4th gives happiness and plentiful fixed assets.

disagreements: Sources agree on difficulty. Saravali and Raman see writing and reading as a compensating gift; Brihat Jataka does not mention it. Braha's lagna-based note for Taurus ascendant is more favourable than the sign verses.
phrasing_guidance: Frame as recognition that arrives through persistence and humility. Avoid predicting estrangement; say relationships benefit from softening pride.

summary: Saturn in Virgo, the sign of its friend Mercury, gets mixed verdicts. Saravali lists dependence, few friends and low conduct, but also sons, wealth, helpfulness and caution; Raman's sign list is harsh, yet his dasa note promises elevation and fame. Foss says Virgo has a particular problem with Saturn.
common_outcomes: Cautious in action and helpful to others (Saravali 29.11-12)
Sons and wealth, with some dependence on others and few friends (Saravali 29.11-12)
Raman lists poverty, quarrelsomeness and conservatism but also a taste for public life (HPA ch.22)
Raman's dasa note: elevation, royal favour, business success and fame (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Brihat Jataka 18.17 (Mercury's signs): uneven in writing or painting, lacking comfort
Saravali 29.40: Mercury aspect gives wealth and skill in arts; 29.42: Venus aspect, a teacher of yoga or saint

by_area.personality: Cautious and helpful (Saravali 29.11-12); Raman lists narrow-minded, erratic and conservative traits (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Taste for public life (Raman HPA ch.22); elevation and business success in Saturn's dasa (Raman HPA ch.24).
by_area.finance: Saravali 29.11-12 gives wealth; Raman's sign list says poor (HPA ch.22).
by_area.spirituality: Foss recommends worship of the Sun (Gayatri) to meet Saturn's difficulty in Virgo (name 34).

strengtheners: Mercury is Saturn's friend (Braha; Bhavartha Ratnakara 15.7 lists Virgo as friendly)
Mercury or Jupiter aspect on Saturn (Saravali 29.40-41)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars aspect (Saravali 29.39)
Foss: Saturn's air opposes the earth of Mercury's Virgo, giving Virgo a particular problem with Saturn (name 34)
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there.

source_views.source: Saravali 29.11-12 (English e-text on archive.org whose chapter captions and wording match R. Santhanam's translation; translator not named in the file)
source_views.view: Saturn in Virgo: crafty, dependent on others for food, few friends, unacquainted with arts, indolent, yet possesses sons and wealth, helpful to others and cautious in actions.

source_views.source: Saravali 29.37-42 (English e-text, archive.org)
source_views.view: Aspects in Mercury's signs: Mercury gives wealth and arts; Jupiter trust and virtue; Mars burdens; Venus a yoga teacher or saint.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 18.17 (tr. M. D. Neely)
source_views.view: Mercury's signs: lacking modesty, comfort, wealth, children; inconsistent in writing or painting.

source_views.source: Bhavartha Ratnakara ch.15 v.7 'Planetary rulerships' (English compilation by Ramapriya, archive.org)
source_views.view: For Saturn, Virgo is friendly.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.22 'Planets in Different Rasis', Saturn (pp.132-134)

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch.24, Saturn's dasa by sign (pp.158-159)
source_views.view: Saturn's dasa from Virgo: elevation to high positions, royal favour, business success, fame.

source_views.source: Andrew Foss, The Yoga of the Planets: Saturn (commentary on Saturn's 108 names, archive.org)
source_views.view: Commentary on name 34: Saturn (air) opposes Mercury's earth; Virgo has a particular problem with Saturn, answered by worship of the Sun (Gayatri).

disagreements: Friendly by dignity tables, but Foss calls Virgo problematic for Saturn. Brihat Jataka denies children and wealth for Mercury's signs while Saravali gives sons and wealth for Virgo. Raman's sign list is harsh but his dasa note is favourable.
phrasing_guidance: Highlight diligence, craft and service. Do not make moral judgements about the person.

summary: Saturn is exalted in Libra (deepest at 20 degrees), in the sign of its friend Venus. It is one of Saturn's best placements: classical and modern texts agree on wealth, standing, sound judgment and leadership of groups or institutions.
common_outcomes: Respect and leadership within groups, towns and institutions (Brihat Jataka 18.18; Saravali 29.13-14: senior in his circle)
Wealth and honour, including from abroad (Saravali 29.13-14; Brihat Jataka 18.18)

by_area.relationships: Saravali 29.13-14 and Raman (subservient to women, HPA ch.22) note strong attachments.
by_area.family: Wealth protected by relatives (Saravali 29.13-14); domestic happiness in Saturn's dasa (Raman HPA ch.24).

Braha: Saturn in Libra in the ascendant gives leadership and high status; Foss cites Margaret Thatcher (Libra rising, exalted Saturn) as an example of leadership and a well-presented style.

summary: Saturn in Scorpio is in the sign of its enemy Mars. Classical and modern texts describe a hostile, harsh and miserly temperament, wealth gained through others and a risk-prone life; it is a placement of endurance under pressure.
common_outcomes: Hostile, ill-tempered or harsh temperament (Saravali 29.15-16; Brihat Jataka 18.17; Raman HPA ch.22)
Wealth, including through others' money, alongside losses and misery (Saravali 29.15-16)
Reserved, adventurous and hard-hearted (Raman HPA ch.22)
Raman's dasa note: displeasure of superiors and loss of prestige (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.15-16 and Raman (HPA ch.22) list risks from poison, fire or weapons (a risk theme, never a prediction)
Saravali 29.15-16 says averse to festive music
Saravali 29.29: Jupiter aspect in a Mars sign gives wealth, fortune and a minister's or chief's position

by_area.personality: Hostile, crooked, egoistic in Saravali 29.15-16; Raman: reserved, adventurous, hard-hearted, rash (HPA ch.22).
by_area.career: Raman's dasa note warns of friction with superiors and loss of prestige (HPA ch.24).
by_area.finance: Rich and miserly, gaining others' money, yet facing loss (Saravali 29.15-16); Raman adds wastefulness (HPA ch.22).

Phaladeepika 9.17 enemy-sign effects in dasa

lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there.

disagreements: Texts agree on difficulty. Saravali says rich (through others' money) while Raman says wasteful. The earlier reading of a 'connection with music' was a mistranslation; Saravali says averse to festive music.
phrasing_guidance: Speak of depth, endurance and handling shared resources carefully. Never mention injury, poison or violence as predictions.

summary: Saturn in Sagittarius is in Jupiter's sign, neutral to Saturn. Classical texts are favourable: skill in teaching and sacred learning, fame through good children and family, few words, and wealth in old age. Foss and Braha both say Saturn does especially well in Jupiter's signs.
common_outcomes: Trusted position with authorities; good children, spouse and wealth (Brihat Jataka 18.19)
Skill in conduct, teaching and the meaning of sacred texts (Saravali 29.17-18)
Fame through virtuous children, family profession and own virtues; affluence in old age (Saravali 29.17-18)
Raman's dasa note: philosophical and religious study and peace (HPA ch.24)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.17-18 says speaks little and has many names
Saravali 29.59: Jupiter aspect makes one a king, minister or army chief; 29.58: Mercury aspect a respected preceptor; 29.57: Mars aspect is unfavourable
Brihat Jataka 18.19: leadership of a town, army or village

by_area.career: Teaching and sacred learning (Saravali 29.17-18); leading a town or group (Brihat Jataka 18.19).
by_area.relationships: Brihat Jataka 18.19 gives a good spouse; Raman notes troubles with wife (HPA ch.22).
by_area.family: Fame through virtuous children and family profession (Saravali 29.17-18); dutiful children (Raman HPA ch.22).
by_area.spirituality: Study of philosophy and religion (Raman HPA ch.24).

summary: Saturn in Capricorn is in its own sign. Saravali gives learning, many arts, honour among one's people, courage and residence abroad; Brihat Jataka gives leadership of a town or group; Raman adds intelligence and domestic harmony, and Foss calls Capricorn steady and suited to big business.

Sasa yoga when in an angle (Saravali 37.2)

Brihat Jataka 18.19: wealth connected with another's spouse, unkempt appearance

by_area.relationships: Raman: harmony in domestic life (HPA ch.22).

disagreements: Strength is agreed. The earlier file put untruthful and indulgent traits under Capricorn; in the Saravali text those belong to Aquarius (29.21-22). Brihat Jataka still gives some unflattering traits for Saturn's own signs.
phrasing_guidance: Emphasise reliability, organisation and earned authority. Avoid character labels like 'untruthful'.

summary: Saturn in Aquarius is in its moolatrikona (0-20 degrees) and own sign beyond, and Foss calls it Saturn's strongest sign. Classical verses are nevertheless harsh (untruthful, harsh speech, many undertakings), while Raman's modern list is favourable: practical, able, diplomatic and philosophical.
common_outcomes: Attempts many undertakings (Saravali 29.21-22)
Eminent standing (Saravali 29.21-22); leadership of a group with steady means (Brihat Jataka 18.19)
Raman: practical, able, diplomatic, ingenious, prudent, reflective, philosophical (HPA ch.22)
Sasa yoga when in an angle (Saravali 37.2)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.21-22 lists untruthfulness, harsh speech, indulgence and aversion to tradition
Raman: can be overcome by enemies (HPA ch.22); his dasa note gives travel westward, success in litigation and wealth (HPA ch.24)
BPHS 3.59: moolatrikona gives three-quarters of full benefic results

by_area.personality: Raman: practical, diplomatic, reflective (HPA ch.22); Saravali 29.21-22: harsh in speech.
by_area.career: Many undertakings (Saravali 29.21-22); Braha: in the 10th, a powerful leader with a vision for organisations; Foss: Saturn rising in Aquarius gives influence over the masses (Karl Marx example).
by_area.finance: Raman's dasa note: acquisition of wealth (HPA ch.24).
by_area.spirituality: Raman lists a philosophical turn (HPA ch.22).

strengtheners: Angle placement (Sasa yoga, Saravali 37.2)
Jupiter, Mars or Venus aspect (Saravali 29.63, 29.65, 29.66)
Degree within 0-20, the moolatrikona (BPHS 3.54; Raman HPA ch.6; Frawley p.127)
weakeners_or_cancellations: Sun or Moon aspect (Saravali 29.61-62)
Combustion (Phaladeepika 9.19)
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman (HPA ch.17) names Saturn the sole rajayoga planet for Taurus and Libra lagnas, so its sign results tend to be felt more favourably there. Braha: Saturn in Aquarius in the ascendant gives leadership and high status. Foss notes the tamas of both Saturn and Aquarius when Saturn rises there.

summary: Saturn in Pisces is in Jupiter's sign, neutral to Saturn. Saravali is kind: fond of sacrifices and arts, chief among relatives and friends, calm, skilled in policy and in judging gems, virtuous and modest, with growing wealth and authority later in life. Foss and Braha both rate Jupiter's signs highly for Saturn.

Increasing wealth and an authoritative position later in life (Saravali 29.23-24)
Trusted role, good family, leadership (Brihat Jataka 18.19)
Raman: clever, gifted, polite, helpful and wealthy (HPA ch.22)
rare_outcomes: Saravali 29.23-24: skill at testing diamonds and in policy-making
Saravali 29.60: Venus aspect, living in forests or hills, unsteady; 29.56: Moon aspect, two names with wife, children and wealth
Raman's dasa note: pilgrimages and indifference to sectarian rules, with some sorrow and unrest (HPA ch.24)

by_area.career: Skill in policy-making; authority later in life (Saravali 29.23-24).
by_area.spirituality: Fond of sacrifices (Saravali 29.23-24); pilgrimage in Saturn's dasa (Raman HPA ch.24).
